question.text: An MFN (Most Favoured Nation) provision in an AIF side letter typically entitles an investor to:

answer.text: Receive automatic exemption from all capital calls during market downturns
A guaranteed minimum IRR of 12% p.a. regardless of fund performance
Vote as if holding 2x their economic interest on all governance matters
Elect the benefit of rights contained in OTHER investors' side letters, and potentially also the right to view those other side letters

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.7.1 (Role of Fund Governance), an MFN provision entitles an investor to elect the benefit of rights contained in other investors' side letters, and potentially also the right to view those other side letters. The sponsor/manager should ensure MFN usage is regularised so special rights are not arbitrarily afforded. The Trap: MFN does not grant capital-call exemptions, voting multipliers, or guaranteed IRR — those would be economic side-rights that violate fund parity. Cross-Exam Context: Same MFN principle appears in XIX-A (side-letter disclosure obligation) and in X-A/X-B for IA client-specific agreements. Manager's Pro-Tip: Maintain an MFN matrix — columns = side-letter rights, rows = LPs. Each new side letter asks 'does any existing LP with MFN get this too?' before signing. Missing this creates stealth parity violations.
